title: Rabbi Joey Soffer: Mesilat Yesharim class #13

chapters.about: Inspecting actions for Niki and overcharging in business transactions

chapters.title: The Severity of Stealing and Dishonesty
chapters.about: The impact of stealing, drought, and adjectives for dishonest people

chapters.title: Weights, Measures, and Charging Interest
chapters.about: Inaccurate scales, wholesale cleaning obligations, and interest as denying God

chapters.title: The Coin on Fire and Guarding Against Money
chapters.about: Fear of God shown through money, the coin of fire shown to the Gaon

chapters.title: Introduction to Illicit Relations and Fences
chapters.about: Desire for illicit relations, the Nazir paradigm, and the fences of the Torah

chapters.title: Guarding the Senses and Avoiding Improper Contact
chapters.about: Looking at women, counting money from hand to hand, and guarding the senses

summary: Rabbi Soffer continues learning in Mesilat Yesharim, discussing the attribute of Niki and the careful inspection needed regarding business transactions. He teaches about the severe prohibitions of overcharging, stealing, false weights and measures, and charging interest, connecting them to a person's fear of God. He also begins discussing the precautions and boundaries related to illicit relations and guarding one's senses.
questions: Why is charging interest compared to denying the existence of God?
How often were wholesalers obligated to clean and check their weights and measures?
What did the Gaon say about using a nail from money that was not coming to you?
Why did the rabbis go out into the field and sit in the trees in the forest to learn Torah?
How are the laws of Nazir used as a paradigm for setting fences around illicit relations?
